[UI] Update Font Size - Flutter Migration

QA Tester Summary

Verdict: BUG
Issue: #1 - [UI] Update Font Size
QA Date: 2026-07-27
Build / App Evidence: Android real-device manual video from QA tester
Scope Tested: Typography/font-size system, OpenSans registration, reusable typography scale, hardcoded widget font sizes, and visual behavior on real-device core screens.

Test Scenario Summary

# Method Scenario Evidence Result
1 White Box Verify OpenSans Regular/Bold are registered as Flutter fonts. pubspec.yaml, assets/ font scan Fail
2 White Box Verify app theme uses the requested OpenSans family as the typography source. lib/app/theme.dart, lib/app/typography.dart Fail
3 White Box Verify font sizes come from a single reusable typography scale instead of hardcoded widget values. rg fontSize over lib/ Fail
4 Gray Box Verify central typography helpers exist and are used by many shared components/screens. TourTypography, TourTextContext, component imports Pass
5 Black Box Verify real-device screens are readable at default font settings across login, drawer, tour list, settings, and create-tour flows. Manual Android video Pass
6 Black Box Verify no obvious text clipping/overlap in the recorded core screens. Manual Android video Pass
7 Regression / Accessibility Verify system text scaling behavior against acceptance criteria. Manual video did not clearly isolate Android font-size increase; source review shows no custom blocking of scaling Not fully covered

Code Review Summary

Area Files Reviewed Review Notes Result
Font asset registration pubspec.yaml, assets/ No fonts: section and no OpenSans .ttf/.otf files were found. This fails the OpenSans Regular/Bold acceptance criterion. Fail
Theme typography lib/app/theme.dart Theme uses Typography.geist(...), not OpenSans. The issue explicitly asks OpenSans to be registered and rendered. Fail
Typography scale lib/app/typography.dart A centralized TourTypography scale exists with documented sizes 14/16/18/20/22 and reusable getters. Pass
Hardcoded widget font sizes lib/components/**, lib/features/** Multiple widgets still define direct fontSize values such as 11, 12, 13, and 16 outside the central scale. Fail
Real-device visual readability Manual video Login, navigation drawer, Real Estate list, settings, and create-tour screens are readable and do not show obvious overflow in recorded default-size flow. Pass

Screens / Areas Not Using OpenSans

OpenSans is not installed globally yet, so every app route still renders through the current theme font (Typography.geist(...)) or platform/default fallback instead of the requested OpenSans family. The affected app routes include Login, Home, Real Estate list, Google Business list, GoThru Listings, Profile, Settings, Street View Account, Delete Account, About GoThru, Create Tour, detail screens, Viewer, Add Connection, and Insta360 Camera.

Remaining Hardcoded Font-Size Areas

The prior review identified direct widget-level fontSize values in About, Settings, Profile, Street View Account, Delete Account, GoThru list, tour list, Create Tour, Viewer/Panorama overlay, menu drawer, Panorama Info, Edit Tour Name, Detail Loading Overlay, and Insta360 Camera views.

Gray Box Verified that a project-level typography helper exists and is adopted by many screens/components, but the adoption is incomplete. Partial
Black Box Manual real-device recording using real account/data across key app screens. Pass for readability, Fail overall due to source acceptance gaps

[Tour Detail] Integrate Add Panorama from Camera 360 (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN connects to an Insta360 camera over WiFi (OSC protocol, fixed AP http://192.168.42.1:80) to capture/import 360° images; see docs/analyze.md §2.1 and §3.5. Depends on the Insta360 Android SDK setup task.

Goal

Implement, in Tour Detail, the "Add Panorama from Camera 360" flow: connect to the Insta360 camera, capture (or pull the latest capture), import the equirectangular result locally, and persist a panoramas row.

Scope

  • Connect to the Insta360 camera (WiFi / OSC) and show connection state.
  • Trigger capture (or fetch the last capture) and download the equirectangular image.
  • Save locally + generate thumbnail/small variants; insert panoramas row (project_id, default level_id, dimensions, filename, pano_id/stitching_id where applicable).
  • New panorama appears in Tour Detail.

Out of Scope

  • Add from Phone (separate task); connections/auto-link; upload to GoThru.
  • Insta360 SDK installation itself (tracked separately).

Acceptance Criteria

  • App connects to the Insta360 camera and reports clear connection status.
  • Capture/import produces an equirectangular image saved locally with variants + dimensions.
  • panoramas row created with correct project_id and default level_id.
  • Captured panorama renders in Tour Detail without restart.
  • Connection/capture errors are surfaced to the user (no silent failure).

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Capture from camera (happy path)

  1. Power on the Insta360, join its WiFi, open tour → Add Panorama → Camera 360.
  2. Connect and capture.
  3. Expected: Image imports, appears as a new panorama in the list.

TC-2 — Camera not connected

  1. Attempt capture without the camera WiFi connected.
  2. Expected: Clear "camera not connected" message; no crash; retry possible.

TC-3 — Connection lost mid-capture

  1. Disconnect camera WiFi during capture/download.
  2. Expected: Error surfaced; no broken/partial panorama entry left behind.

TC-4 — Persistence after restart

  1. Capture a panorama, relaunch the app, reopen the tour.
  2. Expected: Panorama and image persist.

TC-5 — Metadata correctness

  1. Inspect the captured panorama.
  2. Expected: Dimensions/filename (and pano_id/stitching_id if provided) stored; assigned to default level.

TC-6 — Multiple captures

  1. Capture several panoramas in one session.
  2. Expected: Each is imported once, in order, no duplicates.

Platforms: Android (+ iOS where camera supported). Requires a physical Insta360 camera.
Regression watch: Add-from-Phone flow still works alongside camera capture.

QA Sanity Test Summary — 6 August 2026

Verdict: PASSED. Manual validation on a physical mobile device confirmed the Insta360 camera flow works with real camera data. No coding defect was observed in the executed scope.

[Tour Detail] Integrate Panorama Info (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) to Flutter.
Source reference: panoramas fields (docs/analyze.md section 3.3): latlng, heading, fov, width/height, filename, pano_id, level_id, upload state.

Goal

Implement a Panorama Info view in Tour Detail that displays a selected panorama's metadata in a readable panel or sheet.

Scope

  • Open an info panel for a panorama showing filename, location (latlng), heading, FOV, dimensions (width x height), level, and upload/sync status.
  • Read-only display sourced from the local database with localized labels.
  • Handle missing or empty values gracefully, such as when a location has not been set.

Out of Scope

  • Editing these values.
  • Map editing.
  • Upload.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Info panel opens for a selected panorama.
  • Shows filename, latitude/longitude, heading, FOV, dimensions, level, and upload status.
  • Missing values render gracefully (placeholder or ?) without a crash.
  • Labels use i18n and work offline.

Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 - View panorama info (happy path)

  1. Open a tour, select a panorama, then tap Info.
  2. Expected: The panel shows the correct filename, location, heading, FOV, dimensions, level, and status.

TC-2 - Panorama without location

  1. Open info for a panorama with no latlng value.
  2. Expected: Location shows a placeholder; the panel remains usable and does not crash.

TC-3 - Uploaded vs. not uploaded

  1. View info for an uploaded panorama and a local-only panorama.
  2. Expected: Upload/sync status differs correctly between the two.

TC-4 - Values match the database

  1. Cross-check the displayed dimensions and heading against stored data.
  2. Expected: Displayed values match the database.

TC-5 - Localization

  1. Switch language and reopen info.
  2. Expected: Field labels are translated and no raw i18n keys appear.

TC-6 - Close and reopen

  1. Close the info panel and reopen it for another panorama.
  2. Expected: The panel displays the newly selected panorama's data without stale values.

Platforms: Android and iOS
Regression watch: Opening info does not modify panorama data.

Demo by Developer

QA Summary - Issue #12: Integrate Panorama Info

Verdict: BUG CONFIRMED

The Panorama Info dialog renders a Status row with the fixed value Saved Locally. The current requirement is that status information must not be shown in Listing Information; therefore this is a code defect in the dialog rendering.

Test Scope and Environment

Item Result
Application scope Tour Detail -> selected panorama -> Info
Source reviewed lib/components/sheets/panorama_info_sheet.dart
Data mapping reviewed lib/data/mappers/panorama_mapper.dart
Real-data authentication Attempted with the assigned tester account; the session-token step did not produce the token required by the app, so no listing data was read or changed.
Device run Not executed: no Android or iOS device was detected in the QA environment.
Data safety No panorama, listing, upload, or account data was created, changed, or deleted.

Acceptance and Test Results

ID Method Scenario Expected Actual Result
TC-1 White Box Open panorama information and inspect displayed rows. Relevant panorama fields are rendered; status is not shown. The row list includes Status with Saved Locally. Fail
TC-2 Gray Box Trace data from local panorama mapping to the dialog. Metadata is passed from the local panorama record and missing values have a safe fallback. Filename, dimensions, heading, FOV, and coordinates are mapped; location and dimensions use - when unavailable. Pass (source review)
TC-3 Black Box Panorama without location or dimensions. Placeholder is displayed without a crash. The dialog selects - when coordinates are missing/zero or dimensions are not positive. Pass (source review)
TC-4 Gray Box Compare upload/sync state behavior. No status appears in Listing Information under the clarified requirement. The component uses a hard-coded localized Saved Locally value instead of conditional data. Fail
TC-5 White Box Verify field-label localization path. Labels use localization resources. Panorama field labels and status label are retrieved from localization resources. Pass (source review)
TC-6 Runtime Open, close, and reopen Info for another panorama. Newly selected metadata appears without stale values. Not executed because no testable device was attached and real-data login could not establish the app session. Blocked - setup

Code Review

Area Evidence Assessment
Status rendering PanoramaInfoDialog adds (l10n.t_flutter_status, l10n.t_projectDetail_t_tourInfo_t_savedLocally) to rows. Defect: the row is unconditional and always visible.
Real metadata mapping PanoramaMapper maps filename, width, height, heading, FOV, and latlng to TourScene. Correct for the reviewed fields.
Missing-value handling Dialog computes - for absent/zero coordinates and non-positive dimensions. Correct defensive behavior.
Localization Field labels are read through l10n. Correct; no raw key is rendered by the reviewed dialog.

Response / Integration Review

Request chain Observed result QA classification
POST https://apiw.gothru.co/users/oauth/token -> GET /signin/{accessToken} -> POST https://apil.gothru.co/auth/check-session?ec=false The real-data session-token step did not provide the token the app needs to load authenticated listings. No protected listing request was sent. Setup or API-contract blocker; not recorded as an Issue #12 coding defect.

Metadata placeholder must be safe Safe - fallback is implemented True Negative (no bug) 1
Status must be hidden Status row hidden False Negative 0
Status is allowed Status row visible False Positive 0

Confirmed Coding Bug

  • Actual: Status: Saved Locally is always rendered in the Panorama Info dialog.
  • Expected: Status information is not displayed in Listing Information.
  • Impact: The dialog presents information that the current product requirement explicitly excludes.
  • Recommended fix: Remove the status tuple from the dialog's rows collection. Keep the remaining panorama metadata and existing missing-value safeguards intact.
WhatsApp.Video.2026-07-29.at.11.40.33.mp4

Limitations

  • Runtime UI and real listing-data checks remain blocked by the unavailable mobile device and the real-data session-token failure. These are recorded as setup/integration limits, not as Issue #12 bugs.

[Login] Integrate Login Google (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) -> Flutter.
Source reference: RN uses Google Sign-In (@react-native-google-signin) and stores google_token/google_access_token alongside the GoThru session (see docs/analyze.md ?2.8, ?3.4).

Goal

Implement Google Sign-In in the Flutter app: the user authenticates with Google, the app exchanges/validates with the GoThru API, and the session + Google tokens are persisted.

Scope

  • "Continue with Google" button -> native Google sign-in flow.
  • Obtain Google token, authenticate with GoThru, store token/tokenApil/gothru_uid + google_token/google_access_token.
  • Persist session across restarts; route to Main on success.
  • Handle cancel and failure cases.

Out of Scope

  • Email and Apple sign-in (separate tasks); Google Drive backup integration.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Google sign-in completes and creates a valid GoThru session.
  • Google + GoThru tokens stored securely; session persists across restarts.
  • User-cancelled sign-in returns to login cleanly (no error spam).
  • Failures (network / denied) surfaced clearly; on success lands on Main.

?? Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 ? Google sign-in (happy path)

  1. Tap Continue with Google -> choose an account -> grant consent.
  2. Expected: Signs in; lands on Main; session stored.

TC-2 ? User cancels

  1. Start Google sign-in and cancel the account chooser.
  2. Expected: Returns to login; no error toast/crash.

TC-3 ? Session persistence

  1. Sign in with Google, relaunch the app.
  2. Expected: Still signed in.

TC-4 ? Network error

  1. Go offline and attempt Google sign-in.
  2. Expected: Clear network error; retry possible.

TC-5 ? Account with no GoThru access (if applicable)

  1. Use a Google account not provisioned on GoThru.
  2. Expected: Handled gracefully with an informative message.

TC-6 ? Localization

  1. Switch language and view login.
  2. Expected: Button/labels/errors translated.

Platforms: Android + iOS (requires Google services configured)
Regression watch: email login still works alongside Google.

QA Summary - Issue #17: Login Google

Verdict: BUG FOUND

Test Evidence

Item Result
Manual real-mobile validation Completed by QA tester using testpanorra@gmail.com.
Supporting automated check flutter test test/auth_service_test.dart passed: 8/8 tests.
Coding defect Offline Google Sign-In error/alert is not informative, failing TC-4.

Manual Real-Mobile Test Results

ID Method Scenario Expected Actual Result
TC-1 Gray Box Google Sign-In using the tester account. Google and GoThru authentication complete and Main opens. Completed successfully. Pass
TC-2 Black Box Cancel the native Google account chooser. Return to Login with no error toast or crash. Returned cleanly; no crash/error spam. Pass
TC-3 Gray Box Force-close and relaunch after Google Sign-In. Stored session restores directly to Main. Session persisted after relaunch. Pass
TC-4 Black Box Disable network and start Google Sign-In. An informative network error explains the problem and retry is possible. An alert appears, but its message does not clearly tell the user that the device is offline / that internet connectivity is required. Fail ? coding bug
TC-5 Black Box Google account without GoThru access, if applicable. Informative access-denied handling. Not required for the provisioned tester account; source path has a handled notRegistered outcome. N/A
TC-6 White Box Review Google Login UI/localization. Google button and related text render without raw localization keys. Rendered normally. Pass
REG-1 Gray Box Email/password login after Google-flow checks. Email login remains available. No regression observed. Pass

Code Review

Area Evidence Assessment
Native Google flow GoogleSignInService.signIn() invokes the native chooser and returns an ID token. Correct.
Cancel handling Platform code sign_in_canceled returns null; AuthController treats it as no error. Correct.
Token/session persistence AuthService.loginWithGoogle() validates the ID token, gets session/tokenApil, then stores Google and GoThru session fields securely. Correct.
Session restoration AuthController.restoreSession() restores a valid stored session at app start. Correct.
Offline error mapping GoogleSignInService categorizes non-cancel platform failures only as generic platformError; googleSignInErrorMessage() emits generic/signing-key guidance rather than a dedicated offline message. Defect confirmed.
Regression check Focused auth service suite passed 8/8. Passed, but does not cover native Google offline messaging.

API / Session Flow Review

Step Application flow Result
1 Native Google Sign-In returns an ID token. Passed in real-mobile validation.
2 POST /auth/validate validates the Google identity and reads gothru_uid. Passed in real-mobile validation.
3 GET /login/{idToken} establishes GoThru session data. Passed in real-mobile validation.
4 POST /auth/check-session?ec=false obtains tokenApil. Passed in real-mobile validation.
5 Secure store persists google_token, google_access_token, and GoThru session fields. Passed by relaunch validation.

Confusion Matrix

Expected condition Observed condition Classification Count
Valid Google login reaches Main and persists Observed True Positive 2
User cancellation must not authenticate or error Observed clean return to Login True Negative 1
Offline login must show an informative network error Non-informative alert observed False Negative 1
Cancel/invalid state incorrectly grants Main access Not observed False Positive 0

Developer Bug

Google Sign-In offline alert is not informative.

When the device has no network and the user starts Google Sign-In, the application presents an alert that does not clearly state that internet connectivity is unavailable or how to recover. This fails the issue's TC-4/acceptance requirement for a clear network failure message.

Suggested correction: classify native Google platform/network failures separately from signing-key/configuration failures and show a concise user-facing message such as: No internet connection. Check your connection and try again. Keep diagnostic error codes only in debug logs.

Conclusion

WhatsApp.Video.2026-07-30.at.09.58.33.mp4

Core Google Sign-In, cancellation handling, session persistence, localization, and email-login regression passed on the real mobile app. Issue #17 remains failed because the offline error is not informative, a confirmed application-code error-handling defect.

QA Sanity Retest - SOLVED (6 August 2026)

Verdict: SOLVED - the previously reported Google Sign-In offline-alert defect is closed by developer clarification and real-device validation. No coding bug was found in the retested scope.

Evidence: tester-provided Android real-device recording and offline-alert screenshot; current source review.

Developer Clarification

When a user chooses a Google account while the device has no internet connection, the intended behavior is to show a failure alert. The required message is the existing general Google Sign-In guidance: Couldn't sign in with Google. Please try again, or use your email and password instead. The alert is not required to explicitly say "offline" or "no internet".

RT-5 Regression Login screen availability Google account and email/password login controls remained available PASS

Real-Device Evidence Review

The recorded Android flow shows the Google account chooser, successful navigation into the app, cancellation returning to Login, and the offline failure alert. The alert is visible, readable, and provides the approved recovery options. No crash or silent failure was observed.

[Tour Detail] Integrate Upload Tour (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN uploads finished tours to GoThru via /streeteditor/upload-tour (apil.gothru.co); see docs/analyze.md §2.7, §3.4, and the upload-reliability notes in §5.

Goal

Implement "Upload Tour" in the Flutter app: send a local tour (project + panoramas + connections + levels) to GoThru, with progress, pre-checks, and clear success/failure handling.

Scope
